findings.raw_evidence: Archive contains no PE/ELF/Mach-O/.NET binaries, no nested archives, no encrypted entries, no high-entropy executable blobs, and static pattern scans found no Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder/WebView JS bridge/TLS bypass/weak crypto/base64 obfuscation patterns.
findings.impact: No direct evidence of malware was identified in the static artifact.
findings.remediation: Run YARA, ClamAV, and reputation checks in an isolated environment if a higher-assurance malware determination is required. This audit did not upload the archive to third parties.

findings.impact: Confirmation-gated operations depend on ConfirmationManager.submit(), but the repository contains no production call site that feeds recognized speech into it. Requests can therefore remain pending until timeout/cancellation rather than being affirmable by the user.
findings.remediation: Connect the voice/STT result path to submit() only while a confirmation request is active; bind the answer to the pending request ID and test yes/no, timeout, cancellation and concurrency paths.

findings.impact: High-risk tools governed by requiresPin() receive the same voice-confirmation mechanism as ordinary confirmations. The source explicitly states the full biometric/PIN UI is a later extension. A configured PIN requirement therefore does not provide a PIN/biometric factor.
findings.remediation: Replace the elevated voice prompt with Android BiometricPrompt or a real PIN/key-backed credential flow. Bind approval to the exact request and invalidate it after one use.

findings.impact: When cloud fallback is disabled, open_url returns true before isAllowedUrl() is reached. UrlTool then applies only HTTPS plus simple localhost string checks, allowing arbitrary public HTTPS URLs once the confirmation gate is granted.
findings.remediation: Route open_url through isAllowedUrl() or create a separate explicit destination allowlist and stricter policy for model-originated URLs. Validate the parsed URI host rather than substring checks.

findings.impact: Clipboard contents can be returned directly. Equivalent sensitive reads exist for notifications, contacts, location and calendar, while the Python brain can autonomously invoke tool calls. These reads are not in the dangerous confirmation set, so the authorization model is mutation-centric rather than data-sensitivity-centric.
findings.remediation: Introduce data-classification policies. Require explicit user authorization for clipboard, notifications, contacts, location and calendar reads, minimize fields, and prevent sensitive results from automatically entering long-lived model context.

findings.impact: KillSwitch exposes kill()/resume(), and the dispatcher honors its in-memory state, but static repository search found no production call sites for either method. The configured kill_phrase_enabled flag also has no observed runtime consumer. The advertised emergency stop is therefore not reachable from the supplied source.
findings.remediation: Wire an explicit UI/voice/hardware emergency control to kill(), persist the killed state, check it before boot/service restart and before every tool call, and require deliberate authenticated resume.

findings.impact: BootReceiver launches JarvisForegroundService when coreEnabled and RECORD_AUDIO are true. The service is declared as a microphone foreground service. Android prohibits starting a microphone foreground service from BOOT_COMPLETED for apps targeting the relevant modern API levels.
findings.remediation: Remove automatic microphone-FGS startup from boot. Use an Android-approved voice-assistant mechanism or explicit user interaction/scheduling path, and test cold boot, package replacement and locked-boot behavior.

findings.raw_evidence:
compileSdk = 34
    defaultConfig {
        applicationId = "com.jarvis"
        minSdk = 31
        targetSdk = 34
findings.impact: The supplied source targets Android API 34. Google Play requires new apps and app updates to target API 36 or higher starting August 31, 2026 (with an extension mechanism through November 1, 2026).
findings.remediation: Migrate to API 36, then retest foreground services, exact alarms, permissions, notifications, storage and Android 16 behavior before release.

findings.impact: The manifest declares SMS, call-log, phone, contacts, camera, background location, calendar, exact alarms, all-files storage, broad package visibility, overlay, usage stats, notification-listener and accessibility surfaces. The onboarding screen also requests many high-sensitivity permissions together. Several are not needed by the current FileTool implementation, which is already app-sandboxed.
findings.remediation: Remove unused/restricted permissions. Request permissions just-in-time per feature and redesign broad-access features around narrower Android APIs. Complete Play permission declarations where a restricted permission is genuinely core.

findings.impact: The code calls setExactAndAllowWhileIdle directly. Android documents that SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM is not pre-granted to most newly installed apps targeting Android 13+ and recommends canScheduleExactAlarms() before scheduling.
findings.remediation: Check AlarmManager.canScheduleExactAlarms(); route denied cases to Settings or an inexact/WorkManager fallback, and listen for permission-state changes.

findings.impact: The native layer allocates n/2 int16_t elements but copies n bytes into that buffer. For an odd byte count, n bytes exceed 2*(n/2) allocated bytes by one byte, creating a native out-of-bounds write. Even-length PCM input avoids the issue, but the JNI boundary does not enforce even length.
findings.remediation: Reject odd-length PCM arrays before allocation/copy, or allocate ceil(n/2) with explicit handling. Add native tests/fuzz cases for 0, 1, odd and very large lengths.

findings.raw_evidence: logger.i(TAG, "Heard: $text")
findings.impact: The recognized transcript is logged verbatim before being stored in memory. JarvisLogger tees messages to Logcat and a file with 30-day retention. Spoken content may contain personal or confidential information.
findings.remediation: Disable raw transcript logging in production, or aggressively redact/minimize content. Separate operational telemetry from user-content logging and make sensitive diagnostics opt-in with short retention.

findings.impact: CI invokes ./gradlew, but the archive contains gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties without gradlew, gradlew.bat or gradle-wrapper.jar. A clean checkout of this archive cannot execute the declared CI commands.

* Default catalog. SHA-256 digests must be filled before production use.
         * Empty digests cause ModelDownloader / ModelChecksum to refuse activation
         * (fail-closed). Populate from official release hashes before first run.
         */
        val DEFAULT = ModelManifest(
            listOf(
                ModelEntry(
                    id = "qwen3b",
                    kind = "llm",
                    filename = "Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf",
                    url = "https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GGUF/resolve/main/qwen2.5-3b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf",
                    sizeBytes = 2_000_000_000L,
                    sha256 = "PLACEHOLDER_FILL_BEFORE_DOWNLOAD_64_HEX_CHARS_SHA256_________"
                ),
                ModelEntry(
                    id = "whisper-small",
                    kind = "stt",
                    filename = "ggml-small.bin",
                    url = "https://huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/resolve/main/ggml-small.bin",
                    sizeBytes = 488_000_000L,
                    sha256 = "PLACEHOLDER_FILL_BEFORE_DOWNLOAD_64_HEX_CHARS_SHA256_________"
                ),
                ModelEntry(
                    id = "hey-jarvis",
                    kind = "wakeword",
                    filename = "hey_jarvis.onnx",
                    url = "https://github.com/dscripka/openWakeWord/releases/download/v0.5.1/hey_jarvis_v0.1.onnx",
                    sizeBytes = 5_000_000L,
                    sha256 = "PLACEHOLDER_FILL_BEFORE_DOWNLOAD_64_HEX_CHARS_SHA256_________"
findings.impact: All default model entries contain placeholder digest strings. ModelChecksum correctly rejects blank/malformed hashes, so the default downloader cannot verify or activate these model entries until real SHA-256 values are populated.
findings.remediation: Populate authoritative 64-hex SHA-256 values from trusted release artifacts, preferably via a signed/immutable manifest. Do not allow release builds to ship placeholders.

fetch() {
  local rel="$1" url="$2"
  local out="$DEST/$rel"
  [[ -s "$out" ]] && { echo "✓ $rel"; return; }
  echo "→ $rel"
  curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 -o "$out.part" "$url"
  mv "$out.part" "$out"
findings.impact: The shell script downloads Qwen and Whisper assets from mutable Hugging Face resolve/main paths and moves them into place without checking a SHA-256 or signature. This bypasses the stronger verifier in ModelDownloader when the script is used as a build/setup path.
findings.remediation: Pin immutable revisions, publish hashes/signatures, verify before rename, and make the build fail on verification failure.

findings.raw_evidence:
TP="$ROOT/app/src/main/cpp/third_party"
mkdir -p "$TP"; cd "$TP"
[[ -d llama.cpp ]] || git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp.git
: "${ANDROID_NDK_HOME:?Set ANDROID_NDK_HOME}"
cd llama.cpp
cmake -B build-android-arm64 \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$ANDROID_NDK_HOME/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake" \
  -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a -DANDROID_PLATFORM=android-31 \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF \
  -DLLAMA_BUILD_SERVER=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DGGML_LLAMAFILE=ON -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build-android-arm64 --config Release -j"$(nproc)"
findings.impact: llama.cpp and whisper.cpp are cloned with depth=1 and no commit/tag/hash pinning. A clean build can therefore produce different native code over time, weakening reproducibility and supply-chain review.
findings.remediation: Pin exact commit IDs, record upstream SHAs, verify fetched content, and use a lock/manifest for third-party source revisions.

findings.raw_evidence: openWakeWord                       — Apache License 2.0
findings.impact: The local notice states openWakeWord is Apache-2.0 without distinguishing code from pretrained models. Upstream openWakeWord states its code is Apache-2.0 while included pretrained models are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The repository itself also warns in PRODUCTION.md that openWakeWord pretrained models may be CC BY-NC-SA.
findings.remediation: Separate code and model license notices, preserve the model-specific license/attribution, and do not ship the pretrained model in a commercial product without confirming compatible licensing.

findings.impact: create() launches persistence asynchronously and immediately returns a non-empty UUID. If the in-lock running-goal check rejects the request at persist time, the caller still receives the ID and GoalTool reports the goal as created even though it was not stored.
findings.remediation: Make creation suspend/transactional or return a result that distinguishes accepted from rejected persistence. Only report success after the record is durably stored.

findings.impact: resumePersisted() increments activeCount and launches every persisted running goal without applying maxActiveGoals. A database containing more running goals than configured can therefore restore more concurrent executions than the configured cap.
findings.remediation: Apply the same concurrency gate during resume, define a deterministic excess-goal policy, and make active-goal accounting transactional.

findings.impact: The AlarmReceiver catches Throwable and does nothing. Permission failures, malformed payloads, dependency failures and other execution errors therefore disappear without an audit/log record, making automation failures difficult to detect and investigate.
findings.remediation: Log structured failure details (without sensitive payloads), increment a failure metric, and distinguish expected permission failures from unexpected faults. Never catch Throwable silently.

findings.impact: The source path documented as an Android SpeechRecognizer fallback currently returns an empty string after logging; it does not instantiate or invoke the Android SpeechRecognizer API. Offline/alternate STT recovery therefore is not implemented as described.
findings.remediation: Implement the fallback with explicit lifecycle/permission handling or remove the fallback claim and surface the unavailable capability to the user.

findings.impact: install_tool_dispatcher() catches all exceptions and executes pass. A failed Kotlin/Python dispatcher binding can leave the AI brain without tools while reporting no explicit initialization failure from this function.
findings.remediation: Log a redacted structured failure and expose an explicit degraded-health state to Kotlin/UI. Do not silently convert security-critical initialization errors into a nominal running state.

findings.raw_evidence: lint { abortOnError = false; checkReleaseBuilds = false }
findings.impact: abortOnError=false and checkReleaseBuilds=false allow release builds to proceed despite lint findings. Security-relevant Android lint diagnostics can therefore be informational only.
findings.remediation: Enable release lint enforcement and baseline only known/accepted findings with review ownership and expiry.

recommendations: Wire and test the confirmation voice-input path and implement real PIN/biometric authentication for high-risk actions.
Make data-sensitivity authorization first-class for clipboard/notification/contact/location/calendar reads.
Fix open_url allowlist behavior, native odd-length PCM handling, kill-switch reachability, and boot microphone-FGS startup.
Reduce restricted Android permissions and migrate target/compile SDK to API 36 before Play release.
Commit the full Gradle wrapper, pin native/model sources, and add cryptographic model/source verification plus CI security gates.
